summary: The four tomb rooms D3 put in the Rust fixture become authored world cells under content/world/, and fixture_matches_the_authored_world_cells drops its three B6 tolerances so the equality holds over the whole graph rather than the beach alone.

coordination.notes: Branched from origin/backend/b0-expedition-state at 2f51e77. geography.rs is touched in the equality test only; the fixture itself is not edited, so content is written to the fixture's values rather than the other way round. Two files outside the card's literal list are required and are edited rather than duplicated: content/world/processional_ramp.world_cell.json gains world.portal.processional_ramp_to_tomb_threshold (the fixture already carries it, and removing the routes_from tolerance makes its absence a failure), and content/world/black_beach.region.json gains the four cell IDs (native_expedition_port.gd walks region.worldCellIds, so a cell missing from the region never reaches the game). game/tests/black_beach_route_contract_test.gd asserts region.worldCellIds equals a literal five-cell list and is extended to nine honestly. Shipped: three tolerances removed from fixture_matches_the_authored_world_cells -- the world.cell.tomb_ filter on the cell set, the tomb_only escape in the portal-gate check, and the world.cell.tomb_ filter on each cell's routes_from set -- so the equality is total. The one fixture value content cannot express is world.cell.tomb_service_passage's encounter_eligible = true: D3 set it so the terrace precinct's habitat holder answers the wrong turn (expedition.rs::the_service_passage_presents_the_same_territorial_guardian_as_the_terrace), but native_expedition_port.gd derives encounter_eligible solely from a battleEntries[].status of vertical_slice_encounter, which would instead author a second one-time razorbeak encounter inside the tomb and take precedence over the habitat. Authoring that would be inventing content, so the passage carries a future_spawn_socket like the other four sockets and the field stays Rust-side. The equality test does not compare encounter_eligible (nor interaction_anchor_ids, which the port never forwards either), so nothing was weakened; a later card should give content a way to declare habitat eligibility and hold that field equal too.
